display.purpose: The work title on the detail page. One per page, never elsewhere.

headline.purpose: Page titles — 書庫, 我的書庫, 我的書籤. text-wrap: balance.

title.purpose: Row titles in every ruled list, empty-state and panel headings.

prose.purpose: Reader body text. Reader-set 14–28px, line-height 1.6/1.9/2.2, 2em first-line indent, justified inter-ideograph, 34em measure.

form.purpose: Every input, pinned at 16px so iOS Safari never zooms on focus.

label.purpose: Metadata, counts, dates, status, nav labels. 12px is the CJK legibility floor; tabular figures throughout.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The default and the doctrine. There is not a single drop shadow in the system; depth is a tonal step plus a hairline.

shadows.name: focus-ring-inset
shadows.purpose: The only box-shadow in the codebase. Thickens a focused input's border without moving layout; pairs with the bronze border colour.

shadows.name: scrim-light
shadows.purpose: Backdrop behind the bottom sheet — the one element that leaves the plane. 62% black in dark mode.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and border transitions on buttons, chips, rows, icon buttons.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Chrome slide (reader top bar and toolbar), backdrop fade.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Sheet slide-up, toast entrance, the chapter-position hairline.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions and chrome.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Entrances that travel a distance: the sheet and the toast. No bounce, no elastic, anywhere.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Movement is removed, feedback is kept: the skeleton pulse becomes a static tint rather than disappearing.

components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
This is the visual system of a well-made reference edition — the kind of book whose typography you never notice and whose index you trust on sight. Ruled lists, running heads, metadata on a tabular baseline, one bronze ink accent against a true-white page. Crisp, not soft. The register is archival, exact, quiet: the interface states facts and counts things, and has nothing to sell, because there is one curator and a finite shelf.

Two surfaces, one vocabulary. The catalog is an index to be scanned in daylight on a commute — dense ruled rows, aligned counts, comparisons down a column. The reader is a book at 1am — chrome that appears on demand and leaves no residue, and a page whose only job is to be legible and to stay exactly where it was left. Every shared primitive is written once against the token vocabulary and re-pointed by theme, so the reader's 護眼 page and the admin's import table are the same system under different light.

What this system rejects is as load-bearing as what it is. No cards. No shadows as decoration. No rounded-corner grid of equal tiles. No gradient, no glass, no hero metric. Density is a feature here, and familiarity is the point: a reader should be able to use this on the first night without learning anything.
keyCharacteristics: Phone-first. 360–430px is the priority viewport, 390×844 is the acceptance viewport. Desktop widens the measure (720px → 820px at ≥768px); it never dictates the phone layout and never introduces columns.

Ruled rows, not cards. Catalog, library, bookmarks, TOC and the work page's latest-chapters list are one primitive: a full-bleed row with a 1px bottom rule, a hanging indent for the apparatus, a right rail of tabular counts.
One accent, under 10%. Bronze marks primary action, current selection and focus. Nothing else is coloured.
Spacing with rhythm, not uniformity. The 4→48px scale is used tight inside a row and generous between sections; equal gaps everywhere is the tell of a system nobody tuned.
Motion is state. 120/180/260ms, ease-out only, transform and opacity only. No page-load choreography, no scroll reveal. Reader content is never animated — position anchoring has to stay measurable.
WCAG 2.2 AA is a floor, verified numerically in all five colour contexts, with 44×44px targets and a complete keyboard path.

rules.name: The Chrome Is a Guest Rule
rules.body: Every reader surface earns its pixels or hides. Open chrome pushes text instead of covering it; dismissed chrome leaves nothing behind — no bar, no inset, no residue.

rules.name: The Spoken State Rule
rules.body: Selection, status and updates carry a glyph or a word as well as a colour: ✓ on a selected chip, ▌ before 有更新, 閱讀中 on the current TOC row. Colour alone is prohibited — it fails for colour-blind readers and it fails again in the reader's three themes.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Bronze appears on under 10% of any screen and only where it means action, selection, or focus. If a surface needs a second colour to be legible, the hierarchy is wrong, not the palette.

rules.name: The Zero-Chroma Dark Rule
rules.body: Dark surfaces carry chroma exactly 0. The hue lives in the accent; a tinted dark grey is how a product starts looking like a theme instead of a page.

rules.name: The No-Warning-Hue Rule
rules.body: 77° is the brand, so there is no amber warning. Warnings are a brand-tinted surface plus a ⚠ glyph plus a word. Red is reserved for errors and the update marker.

rules.name: The Verified Pair Rule
rules.body: Every foreground/background pair in use is checked numerically in all five contexts (light shell, dark shell, reader light, 護眼, reader dark). A pair that has not been checked is not in the system.

rules.name: The Positive Tracking Rule
rules.body: CJK display headings take positive tracking (+0.02em). Han glyphs at size want air. The Latin display convention of tight tracking — and the −0.04em floor that guards it — is irrelevant here and is never applied to Chinese text.

rules.name: The Two-Character Indent Rule
rules.body: Reader paragraphs are set text-indent: 2em with text-align: justify and text-justify: inter-ideograph. The two-full-width-character first-line indent is the Chinese prose convention and is the single strongest signal that this is a book and not a web page. Measure is capped at 34em (≈68 CJK characters).

rules.name: The Tabular Column Rule
rules.body: Every count, date, page indicator, chapter number and admin figure sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, so a reader scanning forty works compares chapter counts straight down a column. text-wrap: balance on page titles, text-wrap: pretty on descriptions.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If an element needs a shadow to read as separate, it needs a rule, a tonal step, or more space — in that order. A shadow is never the answer. Audit test: if it looks like a card could be dragged, it is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Ghost-Card Rule
rules.body: A 1px border and a soft wide drop shadow on the same element is forbidden outright. Pick the border. Round corners stay at 2/4/6/10px and pill; nothing in this product is rounded past 10px.

rules.name: The Page Step Rule
rules.body: The paginated strip carries no horizontal padding — the side inset belongs to the paragraphs. A padded multi-column box is narrower than the viewport it is paged across, and the step would no longer equal the column pitch: every turn drifts by the difference and clips text at the seam. column width + gap === viewport width + gap === one page step, covered by an acceptance test.

rules.name: The Unambiguous Input Rule
rules.body: The reader takes the same movement from every device and a gesture is never ambiguous with a selection. Tap: outer quarters turn the page, middle toggles chrome, suppressed over a selection or a control. Swipe: horizontal flick, touch pointers only (a mouse drag is a selection gesture and can never turn a page), 44px of travel inside 700ms. Keyboard: ←/→ turn page or chapter, Space/PageUp/PageDown move a screenful, Home/End reach the ends, Esc dismisses chrome — bindings are listed in the settings sheet wherever any-pointer: fine implies a keyboard.

rules.name: The Sacred Position Rule
rules.body: Any visual change that affects layout must preserve the anchored paragraph: typography is a correctness concern here, not taste. The anchor is captured before a layout-changing setting applies and re-applied two frames later. And nothing undoes the reader's own movement — if they scrolled or turned a page while a restore was still pending, the queued anchor is dropped rather than applied on top of them.

dos: Do reach for the ruled row first. Catalog, library, bookmarks, TOC and latest-chapters are all .row or .toc-item; a new list is one of them.
Do put the primary action in the bottom third on phones, and let desktop release it into the flow (.detail-cta goes static at ≥768px).
Do state the number. 共 128 部, 180 章, 第 48 段, 版本 v1 — this product counts things, and a count is better copy than an adjective.
Do pair every colour signal with a glyph or a word: ✓ selected, ▌ 有更新, ⚠ warning, 閱讀中 current.
Do keep all seven interaction states on every control, and keep the focus-visible ring (2px bronze, 2px offset) exactly as it is everywhere.
Do give failure its own copy and its own retry, separate from emptiness.
Do honour env(safe-area-inset-*) on every fixed element, and keep touch targets at 44×44px (40px is permitted only for an inline filter chip).
Do verify a new colour pair numerically in all five contexts before using it, and add it to the frontmatter rather than inlining a value.
Do keep motion at 120/180/260ms on ease-out curves, and give prefers-reduced-motion: reduce a real alternative — feedback stays, movement goes — never a removal of the feedback itself.
donts: Don't regress to default-framework styling: Tailwind's stock palette (#2563eb, #6b7280, #e5e7eb, #d1d5db), uniform 8–10px rounded card grids, system sans at one weight for everything, no tokens, no interaction states. That is the pre-redesign state the user called "too AI"; it is the thing being fixed.
Don't borrow from commercial web-novel portals (起點/番茄-style): red-orange saturation, ranking badges, VIP chrome, carousels, "hot" counters, density as noise.

Don't introduce a cream/sand/parchment "digital paper" body background. The warm near-white is the saturated generated-design default. Warm paper belongs to exactly one place here — the reader's 護眼 theme, where the reader asked for it by name.

Don't build decorated card grids: equal-sized cards with icon + title + two lines of text, soft wide drop shadows paired with 1px borders, gradient accents. There are no cards in the member surfaces at all.
Don't add a drop shadow. There are none; depth is tonal steps, hairlines and one scrim.
Don't use a colour-only state, a bare number as an accessible name, or opacity: 0 to hide something from assistive technology.
Don't put text on ink-faint (3.1:1) or any lighter neutral, and don't let a muted grey carry body copy on a tinted surface.
Don't animate reader content, ever — position anchoring must stay measurable — and don't animate layout properties anywhere else.
Don't reach for a modal. The bottom sheet is the only one, and a confirmation dialog is never the answer where an undo toast will do.
Don't reinvent a native form control, add a custom scrollbar, or round a card past 10px.
Don't write an arbitrary z-index. The six-step named scale is the whole vocabulary.
Don't hard-code a spacing, radius or colour value in a component. If it isn't in the frontmatter, it isn't in the system yet.
